features.headline: Justin Herbert, defense help lift Chargers past Ravens on MNF
features.desc: The Chargers' defense stifles Baltimore's running backs, and Justin Herbert steps up in Los Angeles' first win.
body: BALTIMORE — The Los Angeles Chargers, who had opened the 2026 season at 0-8 and had not won a game since Week 16 of the 2025 campaign, finally breathed a sigh of relief after a 23-20 triumph over the Baltimore Ravens on Monday night.

Not that they didn't have to slug it out to get there. The victory wasn't sealed until Tarheeb Still forced a fumble from Ravens wide receiver Zay Flowers that fellow cornerback Elijah Molden recovered at the Chargers' 46-yard line with around two minutes left to play.

Los Angeles had been off to its worst start since opening the 2000 season 0-11 on the way to a 1-15 finish, but the Chargers scored on their first possession of Monday's contest and never trailed the rest of the way.
The Chargers were physical on both sides of the ball, as they limited Baltimore's run game to a season-low 16 yards while gaining 160 rushing yards of their own.

And they did what they had only done one other time this season — score the first time they had the ball — to set the tone. Quarterback Justin Herbert, who had a season-low 18 pass attempts, finished off the six-play, 63-yard drive with a 22-yard rushing touchdown.
Not only was it the first time since their Week 3 loss at the Buffalo Bills that the Chargers had scored on their opening drive, it was Herbert's first rushing touchdown since Week 9 last season.
And as the evening unfolded, there were likely more smiles on the Bolts' sideline, including from coach Jim Harbaugh and Herbert, than in the first eight games combined.

features.headline: Mike McCarthy on Steelers' blowout loss: 'Needs to stop there'
features.desc: After a deflating loss at Cincinnati, Pittsburgh faces a Week 11 gut-check game at the Eagles on Sunday.
body: PITTSBURGH — In the wake of a 20-point loss Sunday night, Pittsburgh Steelers linebacker Patrick Queen was soft-spoken and introspective as he outlined two paths forward for his team.
"I think, for the most part, all of us are looking at ourselves and just knowing where we could have been better, what we could have done just to stop the bleeding here and there," he said.
"The other way you could look at it is [that] it goes downhill, and we can just keep going downhill the whole season."
Monday afternoon, Steelers coach Mike McCarthy emphatically chose the former.

"This needs to be one game, and it needs to stop there," McCarthy said. "... This is a part of the journey of the season, but it needs to be one game, and that'll be our approach as we prepare for Philadelphia."
After a deflating 38-18 Week 10 loss, the Steelers face a Week 11 gut-check game at the Eagles on Sunday (1 p.m. ET, CBS).

But just because McCarthy needs the loss to be a one-game speed bump in the Steelers' season doesn't mean it will be — especially facing a cross-state rival in a city where the Steelers haven't won a regular-season game since 1965.

And though the Steelers had a history of resilience under former coach Mike Tomlin and posted a 12-2 record in games following a loss of 20 or more points, McCarthy's units haven't rebounded as successfully.
McCarthy is 8-15 in games following a loss of at least 20 points, including a 2-8 record in Dallas. Even so, McCarthy dismissed the idea Sunday night that the loss could turn the tide of the season.

features.headline: Behind Raiders fans' tribute to Fernando Mendoza's mother
features.desc: Tom Joanides' social media campaign became a meaningful tribute when Mendoza scored in his first NFL start.
body: HENDERSON, Nev. — Las Vegas Raiders fan Tom Joanides, 46, had his first viral moment on social media for a good cause.
He went on X asking Raiders fans, who were attending Sunday's game against the Seattle Seahawks at Allegiant Stadium, to stay seated after No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza scored his first touchdown.
The idea was meant to honor Mendoza's mother, Elsa, who has been confined to a wheelchair due to her multiple sclerosis diagnosis.

Watching the game at home with his family, Joanides saw thousands of Raiders fans remain in their seats while celebrating Mendoza's 10-yard touchdown run in the first quarter of his first career start.

Elsa and Mendoza's father, Fernando Mendoza Sr., were seated in a suite, cheering on their son. "The fan base has an understanding that these are people; I'm shocked and elated that it actually happened. I've never had anything go viral ever,"
Joanides told ESPN. "But I'm not surprised that Raider Nation has the heart that it does."
Despite the Raiders losing to the Seahawks 21-13, Mendoza was "super grateful" for the fans' gesture, and it meant a lot to his family.
"On a dark day, that brings a smile to my face," Mendoza said postgame.
In July, Joanides, a Los Angeles native, went on X and wrote a post, asking fans to stay seated whenever Mendoza scored his first touchdown at home.
However, his post didn't receive much traction.
"I don't have a huge account or anything, so I was like yelling into the void," Joanides said.
Five days before the Raiders' home matchup, Joanides went on X to reshare his message from the summer.

features.headline: MLB free agency tracker: 2026-27 offseason trades, moves
features.desc: We've got you covered on all the major MLB hot stove signings and trades.
body: The 2026-27 MLB hot stove was lit just days after the Milwaukee Brewers hoisted the franchise's first World Series championship trophy.

All eyes this winter are on the free agency of two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal. But he's not the only one who will make a splash in the market, with Freddya Peralta, Randy Arozarena, Seiya Suzuki and Michael King among the other free agents to watch.
Which teams will go big to contend for the 2027 World Series title? And who will make the trades and signings that have everyone buzzing?
Below is a running list of notable transactions and updates from throughout the MLB offseason.
Left-hander Tim Hill is staying with the New York Yankees, agreeing to a one-year, $2.25 million contract, sources told ESPN's Jeff Passan.
Reliever Ryan Walker went to the Milwaukee Brewers in a trade that sent right-handers Blake Holub and Gavin Perry to the San Francisco Giants.
First baseman Jake Bauers and the Boston Red Sox are in agreement on a four-year, $58 million contract, sources tell ESPN.
Reliever Evan Phillips and the Atlanta Braves are in agreement on a three-year, $35 million contract.
Jacob Young agreed to terms on a long-term contract with the Washington Nationals, president of baseball operations Paul Toboni announced.
Source: Detroit Tigers agree to one-year deal with reliever Emilio Pagan.
RHP Ryan Weiss agrees to $1.85M deal with San Diego Padres, sources say.
Mets re-sign pitcher Robert Stock to one-year contract.

New York Yankees closer David Bednar, Chicago Cubs outfielder Seiya Suzuki and Seattle Mariners outfielder Randy Arozarena were among eight players who received $23.15 million qualifying offers from their teams Monday.

features.headline: Every MLB team's chance of signing Skubal — and their backup plans
features.desc: Dodger or Met blue? We break down all 30 clubs' chances of landing the offseason's biggest free agent — and who their Plan B should be.
body: Tarik Skubal is the golden ticket in the 2026-27 MLB free agent class. In what is viewed as a weak group of free agents, the two-time Cy Young Award winner is the clear difference-maker, a pitcher with a 2.42 ERA over the past three seasons.
The state of modern pitching is at an interesting inflection.

While starters are throwing harder than ever — with even more unhittable breaking balls and a wider variety of pitches — it is also arguably harder than ever to fill 162 starts in a season, let alone fill enough quality innings.
In 2026, 377 different pitchers started a game — an average of 12.6 per team — and Michael Wacha was the only pitcher to throw 200 innings.
Ten years ago, there were 310 different pitchers who started a game and 15 pitchers who reached 200 innings. Twenty years ago, those figures were 303 starters and 45 who reached 200 innings.
Forty years ago, it was 9.6 starters per team and 52 who pitched 200 innings — and a total of 82 who pitched 162 innings compared to just 46 in 2026.

You get the idea: An ace starter on Skubal's level is a special addition to any roster. Of course, with Skubal perhaps in line for a $300 million contract, not every team has the same odds of signing him — although, who knows, a new labor deal could drastically change how these deals unfold.

With that, let's introduce the Skubal Tiers — breaking all 30 teams into tiers on their likelihood of landing Skubal. And since every team needs pitching help of some sort, we'll include a reasonable backup pitching plan for each team.

features.headline: 2026-27 MLB free agency, trade grades: Offseason analysis
features.desc: We've got you covered with grades and analysis on every winter signing and big offseason trade.
body: The 2026-27 MLB offseason is officially here, and we have you covered with grades and analysis for every major signing and trade as this winter — which is expected to include a labor stoppage — unfolds.
Whether it's a franchise-changing free agent signing or an unexpected blockbuster trade, we'll weigh in with what it all means for next season and beyond.

ESPN MLB experts Bradford Doolittle and David Schoenfield will evaluate each move as it happens, so follow along here — this story will continue to be updated. Check back in for all the most recent analysis.

The Red Sox weren't high on anybody's list of teams likely to sign Jake Bauers given they already have an All-Star first baseman in Willson Contreras, but this signing is an early candidate for best move of the offseason.

The grade reflects two thoughts: (1) that Bauers' breakout — he finished 11th in the majors in OPS and third in on-base percentage this past season — is for real; and (2) that the contract is a steal at $14.5 million per year.

Bauers will be entering his age-31 season, and, of course, spent years struggling in the majors before finally figuring things out, so while there would generally be concern that his 2026 season was a fluke, all the advanced metrics suggest the opposite.
His Statcast numbers: 93rd percentile bat speed, 94th percentile hard-hit rate, 93rd percentile chase rate, 98th percentile walk rate.
Those are real skills that aren't going to diminish overnight and should allow him to remain a productive hitter (he even hit left-handers well, so should project as a full-time player).
